title: geochemR — import, process and map XRD, XRF and pyrolysis data
text: whole deliverable workbook. Commercial cuttings-analysis reports put every method one sheet — group row (SAMPLE INFO, TOC, TRADITIONAL PYROLYSIS, PAM PYROLYSIS, XRD BULK MINERALOGY, XRD CLAY SPECIATION, XRF ELEMENTAL CONCENTRATIONS), analyte row, unit row, QC row, one sample per row bottom depth cuttings interval formation / zone labels. read_workbook() reads layout one call; package ships synthetic workbook exactly form.  One cuttings well four formations: plot_pam() (light hydrocarbons base bar, kerogen top), plot_mineralogy(), quartz–carbonate–clay ternary coloured formation. Three separate tables. Otherwise one wide table per method — one row per sample — lab usually sends. readers match column names case-insensitively, aliases, tell ignored. gc_data() validates construction — unknown sample ids inverted depths errors; XRD totals far 100, values detection limit without <, duplicate rows warnings — spreadsheet problem surfaces import, map. gc_wide(ds, "XRF") gets back one row per sample whenever want - refuses average two labs’ values analyte unless tell . Every measurement row says came (lab, origin = measured / lab-reported / derived), every input file recorded MD5 hash meta$sources, every processing step logged:
code: f  <- system.file("extdata", "cuttings_workbook.xlsx", package = "geochemR") cu <- read_workbook(f, hole_id = "EX-1", lab = "Example Cuttings Lab") |> gc_indices() #> read_workbook(): clay speciation reported relative to total clay; converted to bulk wt% cu #> <gc_data> 65 samples in 1 holes; 3640 measurements #>   methods: PAM (650), SRA (390), XRD (780), XRF (1820)  plot_depth_profile(cu, "SRA", c("TOC", "S1", "S2", "Tmax", "HI")) plot_pam(cu)                                             # stacked multi-ramp pyrolysis fractions gc_hole_summary(cu, "SRA", by = c("hole_id", "formation"), analytes = c("TOC", "HI", "Tmax")) samples <- read_samples("locations.csv") #   sample_id | hole (or well / borehole / station / api) | x, y (or easting, northing, lon, lat) #   z (elevation, optional) | depth_top (or depth / top / from) | depth_base (optional) | sample_type  xrd <- read_xrd("xrd.xlsx", lab = "Lab A") #   sample | Quartz | K-Feldspar | Plagioclase | Calcite | Dolomite | Pyrite | Illite/Mica | I/S | Kaolinite | Chlorite | Total Clay #   -> canonical names via gc_minerals (k_feldspar, mixed_layer, illite, total_clay, ...)  xrf <- read_xrf("xrf.csv", lab = "Lab B") #   sample | SiO2 | Al2O3 | ... | LOI | Zr_ppm | V (ppm) | Mo_ppm #   -> units from suffixes; "<2" -> value 2, lod 2, qualifier "<"; "n.d." -> NA  sra <- read_sra("pyrolysis.csv", lab = "Lab C") #   sample | TOC (wt%) | S1 | S2 | S3 | Tmax  (Ro / VR optional)  ds <- gc_data(samples, dplyr::bind_rows(xrd, xrf, sra), crs = 26914, depth_unit = "ft") gc_history(cu) #> # A tibble: 3 x 4 #>   step          args                                                   time                version #>   gc_data       samples = 65, measurements = 3640                      2026-09-14 ...      0.3.0 #>   read_workbook path = cuttings_workbook.xlsx, sheet = 1, hole_id = ...  2026-09-14 ...      0.3.0 #>   gc_indices    which = sra,xrf,xrd,pam, min_toc = 0.5, rows = 1170    2026-09-14 ...      0.3.0

title: Derived indices — gc_indices
text: SRA / Rock-Eval (needs TOC, S1, S2, S3, Tmax available): HI = 100 * S2 / TOC (mg HC / g TOC), OI = 100 * S3 / TOC PI = S1 / (S1 + S2) (production index) S1_TOC = 100 * S1 / TOC (oil-crossover index; > 100 suggests migrated oil) Ro_eq = 0.0180 * Tmax - 7.16 (Jarvie et al. 2001), NA outside 400-500 degC XRF (oxides wt%; elements converted oxides calculation): CIA = 100 * Al2O3 / (Al2O3 + CaO + Na2O + K2O) (Nesbitt & Young 1982; molar). CaO corrected carbonate, CIA meaningful carbonate-poor samples; oxide lab report counts zero. Si_Al, K_Al, Ti_Al element mass ratios (detrital / clay proxies) XRD (wt%): carbonate = calcite + dolomite + ankerite + siderite + aragonite clay = total_clay reported, else sum clay minerals QFM = quartz + feldspars (+ mica present) BI_min = (quartz + dolomite) / (quartz + dolomite + calcite + clay) (Wang & Gale 2009 mineralogical brittleness, 0-1) BI_w = 100 * (1.5*QFM + 1.5*carbonate) / (1.5*QFM + 1.5*carbonate + 2*clay) weighted brittleness kind cuttings-analysis laboratories report, 0-100; brittle phases weighted 1.5, clay 2 PAM (multi-ramp pyrolysis fractions, needs Oil1 ... K1): Oil_total = Oil1 + Oil2 + Oil3 + Oil4, Oil3_Oil2, Oil4_Oil3, K1_Oil4 Oil_TOC = 100 * Oil_total / TOC SRA TOC exists sample
